newsitem.title: UK: Sterling debt and futures closing report.
newsitem.headline: Sterling debt and futures closing report.

text.p: Gilts ended up with modest gains on Wednesday, not a bad performance given early losses of a half-point and more, dealers said.
The March future settled 6/32 higher at 113-16, just off the contract high of 113-17 set earlier in the session.
After official figures showed annualised average earnings growth had pushed up to 4.25 percent, from 4.0, the future had dropped as low as 112-29.
"We've seen a good firm close," said a senior salesman at a UK brokerage. "We got down below yesterday's lows briefly. That's where the buying was seen."
The March gilt bounced from a low of 112-30 on Tuesday.
On top of the average earnings increase, unemployment figures showed another staggering fall, with 67,800 people taken off in jobless queues.
Inflationary alarm bells started ringing and were far from doused by the Bank of England's quarterly inflation report.
It forecast underlying inflation close to three percent and rising in two years time and reiterated its desire to see a moderate rate rise.
But the market recovered on the view that earnings growth was fuelled by one-off bonus payments, not wage deals.
Angela Knight, economic secretary to the Treasury said there was no sign of any pick-up in wage settlements and no fear of wage inflation re-emerging.
The salesman said he had pencilled in a forecast of 113-28 for the gilt future at Friday's close. "That's not impossible but we are skating on thin ice up here," he said.

All eyes now switch to Thursday's retail price figures. A Reuter poll of economists forecasts headline RPI will edge up to 2.7 percent in January, from 2.5, while the underlying measure will creep down to 3.0 percent from 3.1.
Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said the headline rate would be pushed up byu higher mortgage rates, following the October 30 increase in official interest rates.
Lower food price inflation, benefitting from the pound's strength, may be offset by a smaller discount in clothing, footwear and household goods prices than was seen last year, he added.
The gilt/Bund spread held steady at around 165 basis points, while the June short sterling contract settled two basis points higher at 93.49.
At that level, it is discounting at least 25 basis points, possibly 50, on top of base rates by the half-year stage.
